**(a)** $u=x$, $dv=e^{2x}dx$: $\dfrac{xe^{2x}}{2}-\displaystyle\int\frac{e^{2x}}{2}dx=\dfrac{xe^{2x}}{2}-\dfrac{e^{2x}}{4}+C$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$: $\left[x\ln x-x\right]_1^e=(e-e)-(0-1)=1$ **(M1)(A1)**

Choose $u$ to be the factor that becomes simpler when differentiated.

Let $I=\int e^{x}\sin x\,dx=e^{x}\sin x-\int e^{x}\cos x\,dx$ **(M1)(A1)**

$\int e^{x}\cos x\,dx=e^{x}\cos x+\int e^{x}\sin x\,dx=e^{x}\cos x+I$ **(A1)**

$I=e^{x}\sin x-e^{x}\cos x-I\Rightarrow I=\tfrac12e^{x}(\sin x-\cos x)+C$ **(M1)(A1)**

The integral reappears; solve for it algebraically rather than integrating forever.
